title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Tort Liability Disputes

articles.content_en:
Article 1 Where damage is caused by environmental pollution, regardless of whether the polluter is at fault, the polluter shall bear tort liability. Where the polluter claims that it shall not bear liability on the ground that its discharge complies with national or local pollutant discharge standards, the People's Court shall not support such claim.
Circumstances under which the polluter shall not bear liability or shall have its liability mitigated shall be governed by the provisions of the Marine Environment Protection Law, the Water Pollution Prevention and Control Law, the Air Pollution Prevention and Control Law, and other separate environmental protection laws; if there is no provision in the relevant separate environmental protection law, the provisions of the Tort Liability Law shall apply.

Article 2 Where two or more polluters jointly commit a pollution act causing damage, and the infringed party requests the polluters to bear joint and several liability in accordance with Article 8 of the Tort Liability Law, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 3 Where two or more polluters separately commit pollution acts causing the same damage, and each polluter's pollution act is sufficient to cause the entire damage, and the infringed party requests the polluters to bear joint and several liability in accordance with Article 11 of the Tort Liability Law, the People's Court shall support such request.
Where two or more polluters separately commit pollution acts causing the same damage, and each polluter's pollution act is insufficient to cause the entire damage, and the infringed party requests the polluters to bear liability in accordance with Article 12 of the Tort Liability Law, the People's Court shall support such request.
Where two or more polluters separately commit pollution acts causing the same damage, and some polluters' pollution acts are sufficient to cause the entire damage while others' pollution acts cause only part of the damage, and the infringed party requests, in accordance with Article 11 of the Tort Liability Law, that the polluters whose acts are sufficient to cause the entire damage bear joint and several liability with other polluters for the part of damage jointly caused, and bear liability for the entire damage, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 4 Where two or more polluters pollute the environment, the People's Court shall determine the extent of liability of the polluters based on factors such as the type, discharge volume, and hazardous nature of the pollutants, as well as whether there is a pollutant discharge permit, whether the pollutant discharge standards are exceeded, and whether the total emission control targets for key pollutants are exceeded.

Article 5 Where the infringed party, in accordance with Article 68 of the Tort Liability Law, brings a lawsuit against the polluter and a third party separately or simultaneously, the People's Court shall accept the case.
Where the infringed party requests a third party to bear compensation liability, the People's Court shall determine the corresponding compensation liability of the third party according to the degree of fault of the third party.
Where the polluter claims that it shall not bear liability or shall have its liability mitigated on the ground that the third party's fault caused damage by polluting the environment, the People's Court shall not support such claim.

Article 8 For specialized issues that require clarification of facts in environmental pollution cases, a judicial appraisal institution with relevant qualifications may be entrusted to issue an expert evaluation opinion, or an institution recommended by the competent department of environmental protection of the State Council may issue an inspection report, test report, assessment report, or monitoring data.

Article 9 Where a party applies to have one or two persons with specialized knowledge appear in court to provide opinions on professional issues such as expert evaluation opinions or identification of pollutants, damage results, and causal relationship, the People's Court may permit such application. If the party does not make such an application and the People's Court deems it necessary, it may provide clarification.
Opinions provided by persons with specialized knowledge in court may, after being cross-examined by the parties, serve as the basis for determining the facts of the case.

Article 10 Investigation reports, inspection reports, test reports, assessment reports, or monitoring data, etc., issued by the department responsible for environmental protection supervision and management or an institution entrusted by it, may, after being cross-examined by the parties, serve as the basis for determining the facts of the case.

Article 11 For sudden or short-duration environmental pollution acts, where evidence may be lost or become difficult to obtain later, and a party or an interested person applies for evidence preservation in accordance with Article 81 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall permit such application.

Article 12 Where the respondent falls under any of the circumstances specified in Article 63 of the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, and a party or an interested person applies for preservation in accordance with Article 100 or Article 101 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court may, by ruling, order the respondent to immediately cease the infringing act or take pollution prevention and control measures.

Article 13 The People's Court shall, based on the claims of the infringed party and the specific circumstances of the case, reasonably determine that the polluter shall bear civil liability such as cessation of infringement, removal of obstruction, elimination of danger, restoration to original condition, apology, and compensation for losses.

Article 14 Where the infringed party requests restoration to original condition, the People's Court may, according to law, adjudicate that the polluter shall bear environmental restoration liability and simultaneously determine the environmental restoration costs that the defendant shall bear if it fails to perform the environmental restoration obligation.
If the polluter fails to perform the environmental restoration obligation within the period specified in an effective judgment, the People's Court may entrust another person to carry out environmental restoration, and the necessary costs shall be borne by the polluter.

Article 15 Where the infringed party brings a lawsuit requesting the polluter to compensate for property losses and personal injury caused by pollution, as well as reasonable expenses incurred for taking necessary measures to prevent the spread of pollution or eliminate pollution, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 17 Where the infringed party files a lawsuit requesting the polluter to cease infringement, remove obstruction, or eliminate danger, it shall not be subject to the limitation period specified in Article 66 of the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 18 This Interpretation shall apply to the trial of civil cases involving damage caused by environmental pollution or ecological destruction, except where laws and judicial interpretations provide otherwise for environmental civil public interest litigation cases.
Disputes over neighboring pollution infringement and disputes arising from occupational pollution damage suffered by workers during their professional activities shall not be governed by this Interpretation.

Article 19 After this Interpretation comes into force, cases of first instance and second instance that have not yet been concluded by the People's Court shall apply the provisions of this Interpretation. For cases where an effective judgment has been rendered before this Interpretation comes into force, if a retrial is conducted according to law after this Interpretation comes into force, this Interpretation shall not apply.
After this Interpretation comes into force, any previous judicial interpretations issued by the Supreme People's Court that are inconsistent with this Interpretation shall no longer apply.
